content.user_title: Plan and Review Family Travel Films
content.value_statement: Travel footage often lacks a clear story, reliable source notes, and organized feedback. This skill combines scene-planning guidance with local cataloguing and limited video helpers.
actual_capabilities: Create planning workspaces and guide scene outlines, confirmed context, personal voiceover drafts, preferences, and timecoded feedback.
Catalogue local media with SHA-256 hashes, relative paths, scan errors, and optional ffprobe metadata.
Generate video-only FCP 7 XML from explicit shot plans with validated paths and frame ranges.
Render silent straight-cut MP4 previews after checking source dimensions, frame rates, and frame counts.
Measure export decoding, black frames, freezes, and audio loudness through FFmpeg without rewriting the export.
Probe Resolve and guard XML imports by requiring an explicitly named, empty, currently open project.
limitations: Viewing, listening, transcription, and model analysis depend on the agent environment; the skill does not bundle these capabilities.
Bundled timeline and preview helpers omit audio, titles, effects, and transitions, and support only integer 24, 25, or 30 fps.
Preview sources must match dimensions and frame rates; mixed-rate, rotated, or otherwise incompatible footage needs separate normalization.
The Resolve bridge targets Studio on macOS, but native import, playback, and export remain unvalidated; other editors lack bundled native adapters.

use_cases.title: Shape a family trip into scenes
use_cases.description: Catalogue a holiday folder, identify meaningful events, and develop one scene with confirmed memories and open questions.

use_cases.title: Prepare a silent picture sequence
use_cases.description: Turn inspected source ranges into a technical shot plan, then generate a silent preview or video-only XML for further assembly.

use_cases.title: Coordinate versioned review
use_cases.description: Record timecoded comments, protected material, verification coverage, and project status before handing revisions to another editor.

prompt_templates.title: Start with one scene
prompt_templates.prompt: Use family-travel-editor to check planning prerequisites and help me outline one scene from [trip]. Ask only for missing footage and workspace details.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: establish the available tools and first scene.

prompt_templates.title: Catalogue selected footage
prompt_templates.prompt: Catalogue [footage folder] into a new report in [separate workspace]. Report failed, skipped, and uninspected files, then suggest questions for planning [scene].
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: organize sources before detailed selection.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a picture preview
prompt_templates.prompt: From inspected ranges for [scene], prepare a technical shot plan and validate source compatibility. Generate a versioned silent preview without modifying originals.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: produce a bounded video-only rough cut.

prompt_templates.title: Review a protected revision
prompt_templates.prompt: Resume [workspace] using its status, preferences, and selected feedback for [version]. Define authorized changes, preserve protected tracks, and report verified changes separately from untested work.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: coordinate a scoped revision with evidence.

output_examples.input: Illustrative request: Explain the helper output for one 25 fps shot using source frames 25 through 74.
output: Selected range: IN 25 inclusive, OUT 75 exclusive.
Available deliverables: Video-only FCP 7 XML or a silent MP4 preview, subject to source validation.
Remaining checks: Native import, relinking, playback, and audio assembly require separate verification.

best_practices: Keep originals separate from planning workspaces and use new versioned output names.
Inspect candidate ranges in motion and confirm memories before writing narration or selecting final cuts.
Record the exact export hash, review coverage, unresolved questions, and explicit author acceptance.
anti_patterns: Treating metadata, transcripts, or contact sheets as proof that footage has been fully watched or heard.
Presenting a silent preview or generated XML as a complete film or verified native editor project.
Uploading family media, purchasing services, or publishing a film without explicit authorization.

faq.question: Is this a standalone video editor?
faq.answer: No. It provides agent guidance and local Python helpers; native editing still requires an editor and supported integration.

faq.question: Can I start without a paid editor?
faq.answer: Yes. Planning needs no editor, and cataloguing can produce hashes without ffprobe. Preview rendering requires separately installed FFmpeg and ffprobe.

faq.question: Do generated previews include dialogue or music?
faq.answer: No. Both bundled timeline interchange and preview rendering are video-only. Dialogue, music, and other audio require separate assembly and verification.

faq.question: Which source frame rates are supported?
faq.answer: The helpers accept integer 24, 25, or 30 fps. Preview sources must match the planned dimensions, rates, and frame counts.

faq.question: Is DaVinci Resolve integration fully validated?
faq.answer: No. The bridge probes connectivity and guards imports into an explicitly named empty project; native import, playback, and export remain unvalidated.

faq.question: Does the skill automatically upload family footage?
faq.answer: The bundled helpers operate locally without upload code. Model and connected-tool privacy depends on your agent setup; cloud transfers require authorization.
